title: Genome-wide siRNA screen of genes regulating the LPS-induced TNF-α response in human macrophages
authors: Jing Sun, Samuel Katz, Bhaskar Dutta, Ze Wang, Iain D.C. Fraser
abstract: A genome-wide siRNA screen identified genes regulating the LPS-induced TNF-α response in human macrophages. Novel hits broadly affect innate inflammatory responses to microbial stimuli.

title: Genome-wide siRNA screen of genes regulating the LPS-induced NF-κB and TNF-α responses in mouse macrophages
authors: Ning Li, Samuel Katz, Bhaskar Dutta, Zachary L. Benet, Jing Sun, Iain D.C. Fraser
abstract: A genome-wide siRNA screen identified genes regulating LPS-induced NF-κB and TNF-α responses in mouse macrophages. This study provides a resource for analyzing gene function in this key inflammatory pathway.

title: RNA-Binding Proteins in the Control of LPS-Induced Macrophage Response
authors: Dirk H. Ostareck, Antje Ostareck-Lederer
abstract: This review examines RNA-binding proteins (RBPs) like TTP, HUR, TIAR, and hnRNP K in LPS-induced macrophage responses. These RBPs globally regulate inflammation-related gene expression, impacting signaling and cytokine production.

title: LPS inhibits TRIM65 expression in macrophages and C57BL/6J mouse by activating the ERK1/2 signaling pathway
authors: Xufang Zeng; Xinxin Deng; Yuqi Ni; Hongfeng Bi; Meiling Jiang; Dan Wang; Pengzhi Dong; Yunfei Xiao; ...
abstract: LPS treatment was studied for its effect on TRIM65 expression in macrophages and mice. LPS inhibits TRIM65 expression via the ERK1/2 pathway, and TRIM65 knockout exacerbates inflammatory cytokine production.

title: Tripartite Motif Containing 52 Positively Regulates NF-κB Signaling by Promoting IκBα Ubiquitination in Lipopolysaccharide-Treated Microglial Cell Activation
authors: Pei Zhang; Yimin Wu; Ruifeng Li; Huicheng Lv; Baolong Yu
abstract: This study investigated TRIM52's role in LPS-induced microglial activation. TRIM52 promotes IκBα ubiquitination, activating NF-κB signaling and regulating inflammation.

title: Corrigendum: Macrophage Polarization: Different Gene Signatures in M1(LPS+) vs. Classically and M2(LPS–) vs. Alternatively Activated Macrophages
authors: Marco Orecchioni; Yanal Ghosheh; Akula Bala Pramod; Klaus Ley

title: Transcriptional profiling of the LPS induced NF-κB response in macrophages
authors: Omar Sharif, Viacheslav N Bolshakov, Stephanie Raines, Peter Newham, Neil D Perkins
abstract: This study profiled gene expression in macrophages after LPS exposure. LPS induced a dynamic, time-dependent transcriptional response, with THP-1 cells closely mimicking primary macrophages.

title: Regulation of innate immune signalling pathways by the tripartite motif (TRIM) family proteins
authors: Taro Kawai; Shizuo Akira
id: Matched: NEGATIVE REGULATION OF TLR4 SIGNALLING BY TRIM30α
abstract: This paper reviews how tripartite motif (TRIM) proteins regulate innate immune signaling pathways. TRIM proteins modulate pattern-recognition receptor signaling to control host defense responses.

title: Analysis of the transcriptional networks underpinning the activation of murine macrophages by inflammatory mediators
authors: Sobia Raza, Mark W. Barnett, Zohar Barnett-Itzhaki, Ido Amit, David A. Hume, Tom C. Freeman
abstract: Transcriptomic data was analyzed to understand macrophage activation by inflammatory mediators. The LPS response can be divided into more co-regulated gene subsets than previously thought.

title: Macrophage production and activation are dependent on TRIM33
authors: Anne-Sophie Gallouet; Federica Ferri; Vanessa Petit; Aude Parcelier; Daniel Lewandowski; Nathalie Ga...
abstract: TRIM33's binding to genes differs between immature and mature myeloid cells, impacting macrophage production and inflammatory responses. TRIM33 is crucial for regulating macrophage activation and inflammation, particularly in mature cells.

title: Tripartite Motif-Containing Protein 30 Modulates TCR-Activated Proliferation and Effector Functions in CD4+ T Cells
authors: Un Yung Choi; Ji Yeon Hur; Myeong Sup Lee; Quanri Zhang; Won Young Choi; Lark Kyun Kim; Wook-Bin Lee...
id: Matched: Bone Marrow-derived Macrophage (BMDM) Isolation and Culture
abstract: This study investigated the role of TRIM30 in CD4+ T cells using knockout mice. TRIM30 deletion enhanced T cell proliferation but reduced NF-κB activation and IL-2 production upon TCR stimulation.

title: InTRIMsic immunity: Positive and negative regulation of immune signaling by tripartite motif proteins
authors: Gijs A. Versteeg; Stefan Benke; Adolfo García-Sastre; Ricardo Rajsbaum
id: Matched: The tripartite motif (TRIM) E3 ligase family
abstract: This review examines tripartite motif (TRIM) proteins and their roles in regulating immune signaling. TRIM proteins, through ubiquitin modification, are crucial for balancing immune activation and preventing excessive responses.

title: Expression and regulation of long noncoding RNAs in TLR4 signaling in mouse macrophages
authors: Ai-Ping Mao, Jun Shen, Zhixiang Zuo
abstract: This study profiled long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs) in mouse macrophages activated by LPS. LPS stimulation significantly altered lncRNA expression, which correlated with neighboring genes and was regulated by histone modifications.

title: The Trim32-DPEP2 axis is an inflammatory switch in macrophages during intestinal inflammation
authors: Zhiyan Zhan; Huisheng Liang; Zhuoqi Zhao; Liya Pan; Jing Li; Yuyun Chen; Zhoulonglong Xie; Zhilong Y...
abstract: Researchers studied the Trim32-DPEP2 axis in macrophages during intestinal inflammation. This axis acts as an inflammatory switch, with Trim32-mediated DPEP2 degradation activating inflammatory pathways.

title: TRIM21 controls Toll‐like receptor 2 responses in bone‐marrow‐derived macrophages
authors: Maria Sjöstrand; Berit Carow; William A. Nyberg; Ruxandra Covacu; Martin E. Rottenberg; Alexander Es...
abstract: TRIM21's role in macrophage differentiation and TLR2 responses was studied in bone-marrow-derived macrophages. TRIM21 deficiency impairs macrophage differentiation and reduces responses to TLR2 agonists.

title: DOK3 Negatively Regulates LPS Responses and Endotoxin Tolerance
authors: Qisheng Peng; Jason L. O’Loughlin; Mary Beth Humphrey
id: Matched: DOK3 Expression is Reduced during Macrophage Stimulation with LPS
abstract: DOK3 was studied as a regulator of Toll-like receptor signaling and endotoxin tolerance in macrophages. Its absence increases LPS responses and tolerance, indicating a negative regulatory role.

title: Knockdown of TRIM52 alleviates LPS-induced inflammatory injury in human periodontal ligament cells through the TLR4/NF-κB pathway
authors: Peng Liu; Lijun Cui; Lifang Shen
id: Matched: Different concentrations of LPS induce the expression of TRIM52 in HPD
abstract: TRIM52 expression was studied in LPS-treated human periodontal ligament cells. Knockdown of TRIM52 alleviated LPS-induced inflammatory injury by inhibiting the TLR4/NF-κB pathway.

title: The Emerging Roles of Tripartite Motif Proteins (TRIMs) in Acute Lung Injury
authors: Yingjie Huang; Yue Xiao; Xuekang Zhang; Xuan Huang; Yong Li
abstract: This paper reviews the emerging roles of Tripartite Motif (TRIM) proteins in acute lung injury (ALI). TRIM proteins, as E3 ubiquitin ligases, are increasingly recognized as key regulators of inflammation and ALI pathogenesis.

title: Expression profiling of TRIM protein family in THP1-derived macrophages following TLR stimulation
authors: Mei-Xiu Jiang, Xuan Hong, Bin-Bin Liao, Shui-Zhen Shi, Xiao-Fang Lai, Huai-Yu Zheng, Lin Xie, Yuan W...
id: Matched: TRIM59 was down-regulated by TLR3 and TLR4 ligands in macrophages
abstract: This study profiled TRIM protein expression in THP1-derived macrophages after TLR stimulation. TRIM59 was found to suppress LPS-induced macrophage activation, while its knockdown enhanced it.

title: E3 ubiquitin ligase trim36 targets ddx3x for degradation to reprogram macrophage polarization and ameliorate tubal factor infertility in rats
authors: Liang Shao; Nansu Wang; Yan Yan; Can Zhao; Yali Tan; Qin Wu; Qiongfang Tan; Yuying Huang; Ling Liu
id: Matched: Overexpression of TRIM36 promoted M2 polarization by downregulating DD
abstract: TRIM36 targets DDX3X for degradation, reprogramming macrophages from pro-inflammatory M1 to anti-inflammatory M2. This process ameliorates tubal factor infertility in rats.

title: TRIM16 Inhibits Inflammation by Interacting With and Ubiquitinating TRAF2 in a Colitis Model
authors: Dong‐Liang Li; Li Zhou; Bo Zhang; Shuai Wang; Qing‐Yu Liang; Qiu‐Hua Liu; Chen‐Jiang Qu; Liang Ji
id: Matched: TRIM16 Expression Was Decreased in the LPS‐Stimulated RAW264.7 Cell In
abstract: TRIM16 expression was studied in colitis models and found to be decreased. TRIM16 inhibits inflammation by ubiquitinating TRAF2, thereby suppressing NF-κB signaling.

title: Human TRIM Gene Expression in Response to Interferons
authors: Laetitia Carthagena, Anna Bergamaschi, Joseph M. Luna, Annie David, Pradeep D. Uchil, Florence Margo...
abstract: This study analyzed human TRIM gene expression in immune cells treated with interferons or activated macrophages. A significant number of TRIM genes were found to be interferon-sensitive, suggesting broader roles in antiviral defense.
